requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` is satisfied. I found no gaps in either the implementation or the tests, and no FIXME acknowledgements.

## Implementation

**Initial (mandatory) set** — `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`:
- It builds the subject, cited-requirement, `{impl}`/`{test}` and anchor selectors into `mandatory`.
- It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
- That function calls `terms::dependencies`, which scans the subject text and every contributed input for terminology references.
  - `direct_references` handles Requirements inputs (definition bodies), Rust outlines (comments only), Markdown and other outlines, and Definition inputs.
  - `close_dependencies` expands the references to a fixed point. It uses a `visited` set, so a cycle terminates, and a `BTreeSet`, so no definition appears twice.
- Each name becomes an `InputSelector::Definition` and goes through `source_input`. That yields the full fenced declaration, including the `:phrase:` option.
- `source_input` also applies the access and denial checks.
- `prepare` appends only dependencies not already in `mandatory`.
- Unresolvable terms return an error from `prepare`, so they are reported before any inference.

**Additional reads** — `read` and `search` in `src/authoring/tools.rs`:
- Every `habeas` form (line range, item, requirements, definition) and `ripgrep` calls `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions`.
- That runs the same transitive closure over the newly delivered inputs.
- It returns only definitions not already in the result or already recorded. This is deduplication, which the requirement's "without duplicates" wording allows.
- The tools return the definitions in the result and in `ToolDelivery.inputs`.

**Recording before submission** — `assess` in `src/authoring/mod.rs`:
- It keeps delivered inputs in `pending` and calls `record_inputs(&pending)` as soon as the next provider response arrives, before any submission is processed.
- `record_inputs` deduplicates.
- A submission in a response therefore comes after the definitions were supplied and recorded.

**Marking:**
- `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `assess`, `read` and `search` all carry `{impl}` references to this requirement.
- The closure logic in `src/terms.rs` is marked for `requirements.definitions.dependencies` and `requirements.definitions.selection`. Its text covers the transitive-closure and cycle obligations this requirement relies on.

## Tests

- **Initial bundle** — `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors`:
  - It uses mutually referencing terms, so it covers a cycle, and it asserts exactly 2 definition inputs.
  - It also checks that a distant, uncited requirement is excluded.
- **Terms contributed by a source** — `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` has a term referenced from a source comment.
  - It checks that `terms.ready` is included.
  - It also checks that an unstaged `md/terms.md` is denied.
- **Introduced by a read** — `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` is an end-to-end test with a cyclic term pair introduced by an item read.
  - It asserts the transitive set, once each, in evidence.
  - It checks that `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:` appear as the first two text lines.
  - It checks that the definitions reached the second model request and were not in the first.
- **Tool paths** — `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `additional_read_flow_searches_outlines_and_reads_a_rust_file` in `tools.rs`:
  - They cover `habeas` item and line-range reads, and `ripgrep`.
  - They assert definitions in results, recording, and deduplication on repeated recording.

## Minor gaps

The only gaps are that term-missing failure paths and requirement-glob reads that introduce terms are not tested under this subject. The missing-term path belongs to `definitions.dependencies`, and the shared `additional_definitions` code covers the glob reads. These do not rise to a deficiency.

:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
